subject: Banking
title: ATM Fees Add Up Fast
description: A short lesson to help you apply ATM Fees Add Up Fast.

hook.text: Using an out-of-network ATM costs $3 from the ATM owner plus $2.50 from your bank.

buildup.text: The ATM itself costs about $0.50 per transaction to operate. The rest is pure profit split between two banks.

discovery.text: US banks earn over $7 billion in ATM fees annually. It's a small revenue stream per transaction but massive at scale.

twist.text: Neobanks reimburse ATM fees to attract customers. They lose a few dollars per user but gain deposits worth thousands.

climax.text: ATM fees exist because convenience has a price. Banks charge not for the service, but for the urgency.

punchline.text: $5.50 to get your own cash. ATM fees profit from your urgency.

quiz.question: How much do US banks earn from ATM fees annually?

details.summary: Out-of-network ATM fees generate billions annually for banks, with the average withdrawal costing over $4.70 in combined fees from both banks involved. These charges disproportionately affect lower-income customers who have fewer free ATM options.
details.whyItMatters: ATM fees are a regressive cost that falls hardest on people who can least afford them. Understanding how these fees work reveals how banking infrastructure monetizes convenience in ways most people do not think about.
takeaways: The average out-of-network ATM fee exceeds $4.70 per transaction
Both the ATM-owning bank and the cardholder's bank charge separate fees
Banks earn over $7 billion annually from ATM surcharges in the US

faq.question: Why do both banks charge for an out-of-network ATM use?
faq.answer: The ATM-owning bank charges a surcharge for providing the machine and cash. Your own bank charges a foreign ATM fee for processing the transaction through another bank's network. Combined, these can exceed $5 per withdrawal.

faq.question: How can you avoid ATM fees?
faq.answer: Use only your bank's network ATMs, choose a bank that reimburses ATM fees, get cash back at retail stores with debit purchases, or switch to a neobank like Schwab or Ally that refunds all ATM fees nationwide.
